clue.text: Tackle bloke about right old carry-on

indicators.note: a word placed about others wraps around them, enclosing what follows

blocks.note: rig is gear or equipment, as in fishing tackle

explanation.surface: A man fusses over his tackle, making an old-fashioned fuss about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloke is everyday British for a man; right and old are both single-letter abbreviations placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tiresome and fussy procedure, which a British speaker would also call a carry-on.

clue.text: Pachyderm dropping beginning to obstruct English river

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it fall out of the word
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rhinoceros leaves droppings that block an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping suggests dung; it is the verb, the rhino dropping its O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major European waterway flowing from the Swiss Alps through Germany to the North Sea.

clue.text: Pipeline is large-scale benefit, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of pairs of words

blocks.note: a big profit, with the initial consonants exchanged

explanation.surface: A pipeline project is praised as a big public gain.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas main is a large underground pipe carrying gas supply to a district, so it is a pipeline.

clue.text: Reference work finally abridged

indicators.note: an abridged text is cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A long reference book has at last been shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: Finally is read as the phrase at last, which then loses its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound book of maps that people consult for geographical information, a standard reference volume.

clue.text: Fluttering pigeon welcoming new dawn

indicators.note: fluttering wings send everything into a flurry and disorder
welcoming someone takes them in, so a letter goes inside

explanation.surface: A pigeon flaps about to greet the new day.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn can mean the beginning of something, as in the dawn of an era, and an opening is likewise a start.

clue.text: Some of them pat his elbow and show understanding

indicators.note: only some of the following words is used, a run of their letters

blocks.note: letters running across the four words

explanation.surface: Some people pat a friend's elbow to show they understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To empathise is to share and understand another person's feelings, which is showing sympathetic understanding.

clue.text: Elite ground-breaking tool

blocks.note: first meaning: the best of a group
second meaning: a pointed implement for breaking hard earth

explanation.walkthrough: Ground-breaking looks like praise for an innovative tool, but it is literal: the tool breaks ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both the choicest members of a group and a heavy digging implement with a pointed head.

clue.text: That female cycling in hills, maybe?

indicators.note: the letters go round like a wheel, the first moving to the end
one part sits in the other

blocks.note: pap is a Scottish word for a rounded hill

explanation.surface: A woman goes cycling in the hills, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Paps are breast-shaped hills, as in the Paps of Jura in Scotland. Cycling moves the first letter of the pronoun to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs expressing possibility without certainty, used to suggest that something might be so.

clue.text: Galileo rudely interrupting extremely contrarian student

indicators.note: rudely handled, the letters are roughly jumbled
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
something interrupting another breaks into its middle

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The astronomer Galileo rudely cuts in on a very contrary student.
explanation.definitionFit: A collegian is a member or student of a college, so it names someone studying there.

clue.text: It soothes chaps suffering piles to swallow a clove regularly

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, knocked out of its usual shape and order
taking letters at regular intervals means every other one is kept
something that swallows takes other material inside itself

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding remedy: a cream for men with haemorrhoids, swallowing some clove.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaps here are chapped, cracked lips, not men; piles is a British word for haemorrhoids.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip salve is an ointment applied to sore or cracked lips, so it is something that soothes them when chapped.

clue.text: Drink case of lovely stout

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone orders a drink, perhaps a fine bottle of stout.
explanation.walkthrough: Stout looks like the beer to go with the drink; it is the adjective meaning fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person who is rather fat or heavily built, a polite way of saying overweight.

clue.text: Part of this nameless, backward French city

indicators.note: a part of some words is a run of letters lying inside them
read backward, the letters run from right to left

blocks.note: the run spanning the end of the first word and most of the second

explanation.surface: Some unnamed provincial French town is described as a backwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Mans is a city in north-west France, famous for its twenty-four-hour motor race.

clue.text: Nattering endlessly about computer system

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter
turned about, the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: Office workers chatter on endlessly about the computers.
explanation.definitionFit: An intranet is a private network within an organisation, a computer system for sharing information among its staff.

clue.text: Origin of peppermint sweetie, or humbug

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: A sweet shop choice: a peppermint sweetie or a humbug.
explanation.walkthrough: Humbug looks like the striped mint sweet, matching peppermint; it means a fraud. A humbug is a traditional British boiled mint.
explanation.definitionFit: A humbug is a sham or impostor, and a phoney is likewise a fake person or thing pretending to be genuine.

clue.text: She merits being represented as a recluse

indicators.note: represented here means presented again in a different form

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman deserves to be portrayed as someone who lives alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface She anticipates the feminine ending of the answer, a nice touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermitess is a female hermit, a woman who lives in seclusion apart from society, so she is a recluse.

clue.text: Cry of curtailed desire in buff

indicators.note: a curtailed word has had its tail, the last letter, cut off

explanation.surface: A frustrated shout of thwarted longing from someone naked, in the buff.
explanation.walkthrough: Curtailed seems to qualify desire, but it trims the little word of. In the buff is British for naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Buff is a pale yellow-beige colour, so something buff in shade is tinged with yellow.

clue.text: Challenged, gets help

explanation.surface: Someone under challenge receives help.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or dispute, so gainsaid means challenged or denied as a past tense verb.

clue.text: Fellow contracted rash, or spots

indicators.note: a contracted word is shortened, here by its last letter

explanation.surface: A man has caught a skin rash, or some spots.
explanation.walkthrough: Contracted and rash suggest catching an illness; rash is the adjective meaning reckless, losing its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Freckles are small brownish marks on the skin, so they are spots in the everyday sense.

clue.text: Shift border dividing post-Soviet states and Europe

indicators.note: something dividing a word splits it apart by sitting inside

explanation.surface: A border shift separates the former Soviet republics from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Shift looks like a change of frontier; it is a loose dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a simple straight dress or slip, and a chemise is likewise a loose shift-like undergarment or dress.

clue.text: Non-standard language is turning up in non-verbal messages

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top
a non-standard form departs from the normal arrangement

explanation.surface: Informal language crops up in gestures and body language.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-standard language reads as one phrase meaning slang, but language alone gives SLANG and non-standard jumbles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Signals are gestures, lights or sounds that convey information without words, so they are wordless messages.

clue.text: Wayward monarch drove Tesla

blocks.note: operated, as one runs a car
symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A wayward king takes a Tesla electric car for a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla is the car brand on the surface, but the SI unit in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means straying from the proper course or standards, just as wayward describes someone going off the right path.

clue.text: Find yourself following well-worn track in area around Oakham

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first piece named is placed second

explanation.surface: Advice to someone stuck in a routine in a country town.
explanation.walkthrough: Find yourself means to end up somewhere. Rutland is England's smallest county, and Oakham is its county town.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutland is the small English county whose county town is Oakham, so it is the district surrounding that town.

clue.text: Congenital criminal tucked into free lunch

indicators.note: something tucked into another thing sits inside it

blocks.note: British slang for a freebie, a free meal or event
a person guilty of serious crime

explanation.surface: A habitual crook tucks into a meal that costs him nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A lig is British slang for a free meal or party one gatecrashes; FELON goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something congenital is present from birth, so it stays with a person for life, hence lasting all one's days.

clue.text: Starts to shame indolent mates with exercises

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of these two words
to tup is for a ram to mate with a ewe

explanation.surface: Lazy friends are shamed into doing their exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: Mates looks like a noun for friends; it is the verb for animals pairing, which a ram does when it tups.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are a common abdominal workout, raising the upper body from lying flat, so they are physical training moves.

clue.text: Bones curve when seen from below

indicators.note: in a down clue, viewing from below reads the letters upwards

explanation.surface: An anatomy observation: bones look curved from underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacra is the plural of sacrum, the triangular bone at the base of the spine, so the word names bones.

clue.text: Pale, tense boy ignoring personal hygiene problem

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out of the word

explanation.surface: A pale, nervous lad neglects to wash and smells.
explanation.walkthrough: Tense looks like nervous; it is the grammar term. BO, body odour, is dropped from boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasty describes an unhealthy whitish complexion, the colour of uncooked pastry, so it means pale.

clue.text: Hide contents of garage, car and house

indicators.note: hiding the contents leaves only the outside, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone is told to conceal what is in the garage, the car and the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a classic small British car. House is astrological: each zodiac sign is a house.
explanation.definitionFit: In astrology the heavens are divided into twelve houses, and the Twins sign is one of these divisions of the zodiac.

clue.text: Sadly, charisma is something very old-fashioned

indicators.note: taken sadly, the letters are left in a sorry, disordered state

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lament that personal charm has gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaism is a word, custom or style that belongs to an earlier age and survives as an outdated relic.

clue.text: Periodically using 8 is key, for example

indicators.note: at regular periods along the word, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: even letters of the answer to 8 across

explanation.surface: Someone applies a lip balm at intervals as a key step, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The 8 means the answer to 8 across, LIPSALVE; its second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A key, or cay, is a low small island, as in the Florida Keys, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: Consequently losing face, Italian leaves crime for farming

indicators.note: losing the face, its front, means dropping the first letter
when something leaves a word its letters are taken out of it

explanation.surface: A disgraced Italian gangster abandons crime and takes up farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry is the care of crops and livestock, the traditional term for agriculture and good management of the land.
